title: Decimals: Place Value, Comparing and Calculating
seo_title: Decimals – Primary 5 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Read and write decimals to three places; give the place value of decimal digits; compare, order and round decimals; add, subtract and multiply decimals. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on decimals: tenths, hundredths and thousandths, comparing and rounding decimals, and adding, subtracting and multiplying decimals. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • After the decimal point come tenths, hundredths and thousandths: in 3.476 the 7 is 7 hundredths.
  • To compare decimals, line up the points and compare from the left: 0.6 > 0.58.
  • Line up the decimal points to add or subtract. Fill empty places with zeros.

Examples

Example

4.6 + 2.75

4.60 + 2.75

Answer: 7.35

Example

Round 6.384 to 1 decimal place

Next digit 8

Answer: 6.4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking 0.58 > 0.6 because 58 > 60.6 = 0.60, which is bigger than 0.58.
Lining up the last digitsLine up the decimal points.
Losing the point in the answerPut the point in the answer under the other points.

faq.a: A way of writing tenths, hundredths and thousandths after a point.
Yes. A zero at the end does not change the value.
In money, measuring and sports times.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 3 in this number?
items.e: The 3 is the 1st digit after the point, in the tenths place. Its value is 3 tenths = 3 × 110 = 0.3.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in this number?
items.e: The 4 is the 2nd digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 4 hundredths = 4 × 1100 = 0.04.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in this number?
items.e: The 9 is the 3rd digit after the point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 9 thousandths = 9 × 11,000 = 0.009.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in this number?
items.e: The 7 is in the tens place, so its value is 7 × 10 = 70.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in this number?
items.e: The 8 is the 2nd digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Its value is 8 hundredths = 8 × 1100 = 0.08.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in this number?
items.e: The 7 is the 3rd digit after the point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 7 thousandths = 7 × 11,000 = 0.007.

items.q: In 5.55, how does the 5 in the tenths place compare to the 5 in the hundredths place?
items.e: The tenths 5 is 0.5 and the hundredths 5 is 0.05. 0.5 = 10 × 0.05, so it is worth 10 times as much. One place to the left is always 10 times as much.

items.q: In 3.333, how does the 3 in the thousandths place compare to the 3 in the hundredths place?
items.e: The thousandths 3 is 0.003 and the hundredths 3 is 0.03. 0.003 is 0.03 ÷ 10, so it is worth 110 as much. One place to the right is always 110 as much.

items.q: What is 10 times as much as 0.03?
items.e: 10 times as much moves each digit 1 place to the left: 3 hundredths become 3 tenths, 0.3. Writing a 0 at the end (0.030) does not change the value.

items.q: What is 110 of 0.4?
items.e: 110 of a number moves each digit 1 place to the right: 4 tenths become 4 hundredths, 0.04. (4 is 10 times as much, and 0.40 is the same as 0.4.)

items.q: 0.6 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: 10 times what is 0.6? One place to the right of tenths is hundredths: 0.06. Check: 10 × 0.06 = 0.6.

items.q: How many hundredths are in 0.3?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths, so 3 tenths = 30 hundredths. 0.3 = 0.30.

items.q: Write in figures: twelve and six hundredths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Hundredths need 2 digits after the point, so write a 0 in the tenths place. So twelve and six hundredths is 12.06.

items.q: Write in figures: three and forty-five thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point: 045. “Thousandths” is not “thousands”. So three and forty-five thousandths is 3.045.

items.q: Write in figures: two hundred and eight thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. There is no “and”, so there is no whole number part. Thousandths need 3 digits: 208. So two hundred and eight thousandths is 0.208. (200.008 would be “two hundred and eight thousandths”.)

items.q: Write in figures: fifty and nine thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point, so write two zeros first: 009. So fifty and nine thousandths is 50.009.

items.q: Write in figures: six and three hundred and four thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point: 304. So six and three hundred and four thousandths is 6.304.

items.q: Write in figures: six and fifteen thousandths
items.e: “And” marks the decimal point. Thousandths need 3 digits after the point: 015. So six and fifteen thousandths is 6.015.

items.q: Which is 0.045 in word form?
items.e: The last digit, 5, is in the thousandths place, so read 45 and say thousandths. So it is forty-five thousandths.

items.q: Which is 2.07 in word form?
items.e: Say the whole number, say “and” for the point, then read 07 as seven and name the last place: hundredths. So it is two and seven hundredths.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 0.700, 0.650, 0.698, 0.069. Then compare from the left. 0.700 and 0.698 first differ in the tenths place: 7 > 6. So 0.7 is the greatest. More digits does not mean greater.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Line up the decimal points and write zeros so all have 3 places: 0.300, 0.250, 0.209, 0.310. Then compare from the left. 0.250 and 0.209 first differ in the hundredths place: 5 > 0. So 0.209 is the least.

items.q: Which comparison is true?
items.e: Write both with the same number of places: 0.125 and 0.500. The first different place is the tenths: 1 and 5. So 0.125 < 0.5. 0.125 has more digits, but it is still less.

items.q: Three long jumps measured 3.08 m, 3.8 m and 3.18 m. Which list shows them from least to greatest?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 3.08, 3.80, 3.18. Compare from the left. Order: 3.08, 3.18, 3.8. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: Three beetles are 1.25 cm, 1.205 cm and 1.3 cm long. Which list shows them from least to greatest?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 1.250, 1.205, 1.300. Compare from the left. Order: 1.205, 1.25, 1.3. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: In a 60-metre race, three runners finished in 9.87 seconds, 9.8 seconds and 9.807 seconds. Which list shows them from least to greatest?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 9.870, 9.800, 9.807. Compare from the left. Order: 9.8, 9.807, 9.87. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: Three apples weigh 0.215 kg, 0.25 kg and 0.2 kg. Which list shows them from greatest to least?
items.e: Write them with the same number of places: 0.215, 0.250, 0.200. Compare from the left. Order: 0.25, 0.215, 0.2. The number with more digits is not always greater.

items.q: Which number is between 0.6 and 0.7?
items.e: 0.6 = 0.60 and 0.7 = 0.70. A number between them has 6 tenths and more after it: 0.68 = 6 tenths 8 hundredths. 0.068 has 0 tenths, so it is less than 0.6.

items.q: Babatunde says 0.125 is greater than 0.5 because 125 is greater than 5. Is he right?
items.e: Compare place by place, not the digits as whole numbers. 0.5 = 0.500. Tenths: 1 < 5, so 0.125 < 0.5. Babatunde is not right.

items.q: Which number is not equal to 0.7?
items.e: 0.70 and 0.700 only add zeros at the end, and 710 is 7 tenths, so they all equal 0.7. 0.07 is 7 hundredths, 10 times smaller.

items.q: Round 3.46 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 3.46 is between 3.4 and 3.5. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 3.5.

items.q: Round 7.38 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 7.38 is between 7 and 8. Look at the digit just to the right of the units place: 3. 3 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 7.

items.q: Round 2.735 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 2.735 is between 2.73 and 2.74. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 2.74.

items.q: Round 0.65 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 0.65 is between 0.6 and 0.7. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. Answer: 0.7.

items.q: Round 4.96 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 4.96 is between 4.9 and 5.0. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. The tenths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 4.9 + 0.1 = 5.0. Answer: 5.0. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the tenth.

items.q: Round 3.995 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 3.995 is between 3.99 and 4.00. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 5. It is exactly halfway, and 5 rounds up. The hundredths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 3.99 + 0.01 = 4.00. Answer: 4.00. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the hundredth.

items.q: Round 6.849 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 6.849 is between 6.8 and 6.9. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 4. 4 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 6.8. Do not round in steps (6.849 → 6.85 → 6.9). Look only at the hundredths digit.

items.q: Round 0.462 to the nearest hundredth.
items.e: To the nearest hundredth, 0.462 is between 0.46 and 0.47. Look at the digit just to the right of the hundredths place: 2. 2 is less than 5, so round down. Answer: 0.46.

items.q: Round 12.508 to the nearest whole number.
items.e: To the nearest whole number, 12.508 is between 12 and 13. Look at the digit just to the right of the units place: 5. 5 is 5 or more, so round up. Answer: 13.

items.q: Round 9.96 to the nearest tenth.
items.e: To the nearest tenth, 9.96 is between 9.9 and 10.0. Look at the digit just to the right of the tenths place: 6. 6 is 5 or more, so round up. The tenths digit is 9, so adding 1 regroups: 9.9 + 0.1 = 10.0. Answer: 10.0. Keep the 0 at the end to show the number is rounded to the tenth.

items.q: To add 3.6 + 2.45, you write 3.6 with two decimal places. Which number is equal to 3.6?
items.e: A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 3.6 = 3 units and 6 tenths = 3.60. 3.06 is wrong: it moves the 6 to the hundredths place.

items.q: To find 12 + 4.75, you can write 12 with a decimal point. Which number is equal to 12?
items.e: A whole number has its decimal point after the units digit, so 12 = 12.00. Then the 2 units sit over the 4 units.

items.q: Chidi lined up the last digits and got 2.81. What is the correct sum?
items.e: Line up the decimal points, not the last digits: 3.60 + 2.45. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 6 + 4 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 unit. Units: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Answer: 6.05. Estimate: 4 + 2 = 6, so 2.81 is far too small.

items.q: Uche lined up the last digits and got 2.53. What is the correct sum?
items.e: 15 is a whole number, so its point is after the 5: 15 = 15.00 (not 1.5). Line up the points: 15.00 + 2.38. Hundredths: 0 + 8 = 8. Tenths: 0 + 3 = 3. Units: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 17.38.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7.3 as 7.30. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 3 = 7. Units: 1 + 7 = 8. Answer: 8.75. Check: 8.75 − 7.3 = 1.45.

items.q: What is 4.2 + 7.16?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 4.2 as 4.20. Hundredths: 0 + 6 = 6. Tenths: 2 + 1 = 3. Units: 4 + 7 = 11, write 11. Answer: 11.36. Check: 11.36 − 7.16 = 4.2.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6.5 as 6.50. Hundredths: 0 + 3 = 3. Tenths: 5 + 4 = 9. Units: 6 + 2 = 8. Answer: 8.93. Check: 8.93 − 2.43 = 6.5.

items.q: What is 0.3 + 6.06?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 0.3 as 0.30. Hundredths: 0 + 6 = 6. Tenths: 3 + 0 = 3. Units: 0 + 6 = 6. Answer: 6.36. Check: 6.36 − 6.06 = 0.3.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 0.8 as 0.80. Hundredths: 0 + 1 = 1. Tenths: 8 + 1 = 9. Units: 0 + 8 = 8. Answer: 8.91. Check: 8.91 − 8.11 = 0.8.

items.q: What is 0.62 + 6.2?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 6.2 as 6.20. Hundredths: 2 + 0 = 2. Tenths: 6 + 2 = 8. Units: 0 + 6 = 6. Answer: 6.82. Check: 6.82 − 6.2 = 0.62.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7.3 as 7.30. Hundredths: 0 + 6 = 6. Tenths: 3 + 3 = 6. Units: 7 + 0 = 7. Answer: 7.66. Check: 7.66 − 0.36 = 7.3.

items.q: What is 1.74 + 8?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8 as 8.00. Hundredths: 4 + 0 = 4. Tenths: 7 + 0 = 7. Units: 1 + 8 = 9. Answer: 9.74. Check: 9.74 − 8 = 1.74.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 1 as 1.00. Hundredths: 9 + 0 = 9. Tenths: 5 + 0 = 5. Units: 1 + 1 = 2. Answer: 2.59. Check: 2.59 − 1 = 1.59.
Line up the decimal points. Write 69.7 as 69.70. Hundredths: 0 + 3 = 3. Tenths: 7 + 2 = 9. Units: 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 6 + 1 = 7. Answer: 77.93. Check: 77.93 − 8.23 = 69.7.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 83.6 as 83.60. Hundredths: 0 + 7 = 7. Tenths: 6 + 3 = 9. Units: 3 + 2 = 5. Tens: bring down 8. Answer: 85.97. Check: 85.97 − 2.37 = 83.6.
Line up the decimal points. Write 7.4 as 7.40. Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 + 3 = 7. Units: 7 + 3 = 10, write 0 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 1 = 4. Answer: 40.75. Check: 40.75 − 33.35 = 7.4.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7.4 as 7.40. Hundredths: 5 + 0 = 5. Tenths: 5 + 4 = 9. Units: 9 + 7 = 16, write 6 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 1 = 4. Answer: 46.95. Check: 46.95 − 7.4 = 39.55.

items.q: What is 1.66 + 53?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 53 as 53.00. Hundredths: 6 + 0 = 6. Tenths: 6 + 0 = 6. Units: 1 + 3 = 4. Tens: bring down 5. Answer: 54.66. Check: 54.66 − 53 = 1.66.

items.q: Add.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 20.3 as 20.30. Hundredths: 9 + 0 = 9. Tenths: 5 + 3 = 8. Units: 0 + 0 = 0. Tens: 1 + 2 = 3. Answer: 30.89. Check: 30.89 − 20.3 = 10.59.
Line up the decimal points. Write 25.2 as 25.20. Hundredths: 8 + 0 = 8. Tenths: 1 + 2 = 3. Units: 0 + 5 = 5. Tens: 2 + 2 = 4. Answer: 45.38. Check: 45.38 − 25.2 = 20.18.

items.q: To find 5 − 2.37, how should you write 5 so both numbers have hundredths?
items.e: 5 is 5 units, and its decimal point is after the 5. Write 5.00: two zeros hold the tenths and hundredths places. Then 5.00 − 2.37 = 2.63.

items.q: Bola found 8.2 − 3.45 = 4.75. Which addition checks her answer?
items.e: Addition undoes subtraction. Add the answer to the number taken away: 4.75 + 3.45 = 8.20 = 8.2. You get back the starting number, so her answer is right.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 5 as 5.00. Hundredths: 0 − 7 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 unit: the units become 4, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 7 = 3. Tenths: 9 − 3 = 6. Units: 4 − 2 = 2. Answer: 2.63. Check: 2.63 + 2.37 = 5.

items.q: What is 8.2 − 3.45?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 8.2 as 8.20. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 1 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 11 − 4 = 7. Units: 7 − 3 = 4. Answer: 4.75. Check: 4.75 + 3.45 = 8.2.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 10 as 10.00. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 ten: the tens become 0, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 6 = 3. Units: 9 − 4 = 5. Answer: 5.35. Check: 5.35 + 4.65 = 10.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 3 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 unit: the units become 5, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 13. 13 − 8 = 5. Tenths: 9 − 4 = 5. Units: 5 − 2 = 3. Answer: 3.55. Check: 3.55 + 2.48 = 6.03.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 7.4 as 7.40. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 3 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 8 = 5. Units: 6 − 2 = 4. Answer: 4.55. Check: 4.55 + 2.85 = 7.4.

items.q: What is 12 − 7.08?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 12 as 12.00. Hundredths: 0 − 8 needs a regroup, but the next place is 0. Regroup 1 unit: the units become 1, each 0 becomes 9, and the hundredths become 10. 10 − 8 = 2. Tenths: 9 − 0 = 9. Units: 1 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 11 − 7 = 4. Answer: 4.92. Check: 4.92 + 7.08 = 12.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 7 − 1 = 6. Tenths: 6 − 3 = 3. Units: 1 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 11 − 8 = 3. Tens: 5 − 5 = 0. Answer: 3.36. Check: 3.36 + 58.31 = 61.67.

items.q: What is 9.9 − 0.79?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 9.9 as 9.90. Hundredths: 0 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 9 = 1. Tenths: 8 − 7 = 1. Units: bring down 9. Answer: 9.11. Check: 9.11 + 0.79 = 9.9.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 1 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 11 − 8 = 3. Tenths: 1 − 0 = 1. Units: 2 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 12 − 9 = 3. Tens: bring down 5. Answer: 53.13. Check: 53.13 + 9.08 = 62.21.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 15 − 7 = 8. Tenths: 2 − 8 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 12 − 8 = 4. Units: 5 − 4 = 1. Tens: bring down 6. Answer: 61.48. Check: 61.48 + 4.87 = 66.35.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 8 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 18 − 9 = 9. Tenths: 5 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 6 = 9. Units: 3 − 2 = 1. Tens: 6 − 6 = 0. Answer: 1.99. Check: 1.99 + 62.69 = 64.68.

items.q: What is 9.5 − 8.95?
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 9.5 as 9.50. Hundredths: 0 − 5 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 14 − 9 = 5. Units: 8 − 8 = 0. Answer: 0.55. Check: 0.55 + 8.95 = 9.5.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 94 as 94.0. Tenths: 0 − 2 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 10 − 2 = 8. Units: 3 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 13 − 9 = 4. Tens: bring down 8. Answer: 84.8. Check: 84.8 + 9.2 = 94.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 4 − 2 = 2. Tenths: 5 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 7 = 8. Units: 4 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 14 − 7 = 7. Tens: bring down 5. Answer: 57.82. Check: 57.82 + 7.72 = 65.54.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Write 24.6 as 24.60. Hundredths: 0 − 4 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 4 = 6. Tenths: 5 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 15 − 6 = 9. Units: 3 − 9 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 13 − 9 = 4. Tens: bring down 1. Answer: 14.96. Check: 14.96 + 9.64 = 24.6.

Line up the decimal points. Write 99.4 as 99.40. Hundredths: 0 − 3 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 10 − 3 = 7. Tenths: 3 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 one becomes 10 tenths: 13 − 6 = 7. Units: 8 − 5 = 3. Tens: bring down 9. Answer: 93.77. Check: 93.77 + 5.63 = 99.4.

items.q: Subtract.
items.e: Line up the decimal points. Tenths: 4 − 3 = 1. Units: 1 − 6 needs a regroup. 1 ten becomes 10 units: 11 − 6 = 5. Tens: bring down 7. Answer: 75.1. Check: 75.1 + 6.3 = 81.4.

Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 6 − 7 needs a regroup. 1 tenth becomes 10 hundredths: 16 − 7 = 9. Tenths: 4 − 3 = 1. Units: 8 − 5 = 3. Tens: 7 − 6 = 1. Answer: 13.19. Check: 13.19 + 65.37 = 78.56.
Estimate: 2.36 is about 2, and 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is about 8. 2.36 has 2 decimal places, so the product has 2: 944 → 9.44.
Estimate: 3.08 is about 3, and 7 × 3 = 21, so the answer is about 21. 3.08 has 2 decimal places, so the product has 2: 2,156 → 21.56.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 1.25 is about 1, and 6 × 1 = 6. Multiply as whole numbers: 6 × 125 = 750. 1.25 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 7.50 = 7.5.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 4.67 is about 5, and 3 × 5 = 15. Multiply as whole numbers: 3 × 467 = 1,401. 4.67 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 14.01.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 0.45 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 8. Multiply as whole numbers: 8 × 45 = 360. 0.45 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 3.60 = 3.6.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 2.38 is about 2, and 5 × 2 = 10. Multiply as whole numbers: 5 × 238 = 1,190. 2.38 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 11.90 = 11.9.

items.q: Multiply.
items.e: Estimate: 0.7 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 9. Multiply as whole numbers: 9 × 7 = 63. 0.7 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 6.3.

items.q: What is 4 × 3.6?
items.e: Estimate: 3.6 is about 4, and 4 × 4 = 16. Multiply as whole numbers: 4 × 36 = 144. 3.6 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 14.4.

items.q: What is 7 × 0.08?
items.e: Estimate: 0.08 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 7. Multiply as whole numbers: 7 × 8 = 56. 0.08 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 0.56.

items.q: What is 6 × 12.5?
items.e: Estimate: 12.5 is about 12, and 6 × 12 = 72. Multiply as whole numbers: 6 × 125 = 750. 12.5 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 75.0 = 75.

items.q: What is 2 × 5.06?
items.e: Estimate: 5.06 is about 5, and 2 × 5 = 10. Multiply as whole numbers: 2 × 506 = 1,012. 5.06 has 2 decimal places, so the product has them too: 10.12.

items.q: What is 3 × 0.9?
items.e: Estimate: 0.9 is less than 1, so the answer is less than 3. Multiply as whole numbers: 3 × 9 = 27. 0.9 has 1 decimal place, so the product has it too: 2.7.

items.q: Without multiplying, which is true about 8 × 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 is less than 1, so 8 × 0.5 is less than 8 × 1 = 8. Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller. (8 × 0.5 is half of 8: 4.)

items.q: Which product is greater than 6?
items.e: Compare the other factor with 1. Only 1.2 is more than 1, so only 6 × 1.2 is more than 6 (it is 7.2). 6 × 1 is exactly 6, and 6 × 0.9 and 6 × 0.5 are less than 6.

items.q: Work out 2.02 × 2.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers, then put back the same number of decimal places: 4.04.

items.q: Work out 4.42 × 3.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers, then put back the same number of decimal places: 13.26.

items.q: Work out 9.35 × 2.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers, then put back the same number of decimal places: 18.7.

items.q: Work out 8.5 × 4.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers, then put back the same number of decimal places: 34.

items.q: Work out 28.2 × 4.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers, then put back the same number of decimal places: 112.8.

items.q: Work out 4.36 × 5.
items.e: Multiply as whole numbers, then put back the same number of decimal places: 21.8.
